description_full: SPIE SA provides multi-technical services in the areas of energy and communications in France, Germany, the Netherlands, and internationally. It operates through five segments: France, Germany, North-Western Europe, Central Europe, and Global Services Energy. The company provides design, ICT consultancy and engineering, installation, maintenance and maintenance durability, technical facility management, and managed services. It also offers E-Mobility, smart packing, barriers, smart FM 360, energy efficiency, modernization, maintid, fabloop, IoT and data management, control room, ergonomie, and cybersecurity products. SPIE SA was founded in 1900 and is headquartered in Cergy-Pontoise, France.

financial_summary: Spie SA is a mid-cap industrials business with a $8.7B market cap on $11.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 86% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $895M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 5.03× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.7×.

Shareholder yield is only 2.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
